headline: SPOT GOLD CRASHES BELOW $4,000 AS CPI SHOCK SELLOFF DEEPENS — Newmont slides 5.1%, silver holds near $51
snippet: Spot gold broke below US$4,000 per ounce on November 12 — the first time in weeks — as Monday's hotter-than-expected CPI data continued to pressure the metal, sending Newmont down approximately 5.1% to around $118.79 and dragging other senior miners lower. Silver held more firmly near $51–52 per ounce, with the gold/silver ratio widening back toward levels that preceded last week's sharp silver outperformance, suggesting retail buyers may be stepping in at the discount.

headline: TUDOR GOLD HITS 9.0 G/T OVER 9.5M AT TREATY CREEK — new high-grade zone 500M NW of main Perfectstorm resource, Golden Triangle BC
snippet: Tudor Gold (TSX-V: TUD) reported that hole PS-26-36 at its 80%-owned Treaty Creek Project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle intersected 9.00 g/t gold and 9.66 g/t silver over 9.50 metres, located approximately 500 metres northwest of prior drilling at the established Perfectstorm Zone. The result opens a new high-grade vector on a project already hosting one of the largest undeveloped gold deposits in North America, suggesting the mineralizing system is broader than the known resource footprint.

headline: ALTIUS AGREES TO BUY TNR GOLD IN C$122M ROYALTY DEAL — locks in Los Azules copper + Mariana lithium royalties in Argentina
snippet: Altius Minerals agreed on November 11 to acquire the approximately 87% of TNR Gold it does not already own in a deal valued at C$122 million (US$86 million), consolidating royalties over McEwen Copper's Los Azules porphyry copper project in San Juan, Argentina — hosting 10.2 billion pounds of proven and probable copper reserves — and Ganfeng's Mariana lithium brine project in the same province. The transaction delivers Altius leveraged exposure to two of the highest-profile copper and lithium development projects in South America under a single royalty portfolio, with no operating risk.

headline: NOVAGOLD SETS DEC 1 DONLIN GOLD CLOSE — NYSE 'NG' listing starts Dec 2 as TSX delists on $4.2B deal
snippet: NovaGold announced on November 10 that its acquisition of Paulson's 40% interest in Donlin Gold — the Alaska gold project hosting 39 million ounces of measured and indicated resources in the top tier of undeveloped gold deposits globally — is expected to close December 1, 2026, with NYSE trading under the ticker 'NG' commencing December 2 and TSX delisting occurring simultaneously. The US$4.2 billion all-share deal transforms NovaGold into a 100%-owned gold development company focused exclusively on advancing Donlin toward a production decision.

headline: CRITICAL METALS ACHIEVES 100% TANBREEZ — $264.5M cash, 2027 roadmap targets first rare earth processing facility outside China
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) reported on November 11 that it has delivered all 2026 corporate objectives: completing its acquisition of European Lithium to gain 100% ownership of Tanbreez in Greenland — the world's largest rare earth mineral endowment by contained tonnage — while holding US$264.5 million in cash. The company's 2027 roadmap targets initiating engineering and permitting for a rare earth processing facility, positioning CRML as a primary candidate to supply heavy rare earth elements from a non-Chinese source as Washington accelerates critical mineral supply-chain diversification.

headline: USA RARE EARTH HITS TWO MILESTONES — Pentagon begins paying on offtake agreement, yttrium oxide samples delivered
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) announced two operational milestones on November 11: it began receiving payments under its Pentagon-backed rare earth carbonate offtake agreement, and separately delivered first yttrium oxide samples — a critical heavy rare earth element used in display screens, medical imaging, and high-temperature superconductors. The milestones mark USAR's transition from development-stage to initial revenue generation, reinforcing the Serra Verde thesis that drove a Jefferies $21 Buy target and an 11% single-day stock recovery earlier in the week.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES 1.8% TO $6.35/LB ON AI OPTIMISM — China physical squeeze intact as ING cautions correction may not be over
snippet: Copper futures recovered 1.8% to US$6.35 per pound on November 12 as improved sentiment around AI-driven data centre demand combined with ongoing physical tightness in China — where SHFE warehouse stocks have fallen over 75% from their 2026 peak — to lift the metal from recent lows. ING analysts cautioned the bounce does not necessarily signal the end of the broader correction, as macro uncertainty from US inflation data and Fed rate-hike expectations continues to suppress risk appetite in base metals despite the fundamental supply squeeze.

headline: GOLD MINERS RISE AS BULLION RECOVERS FROM CPI SHOCK — Newmont +1.6%, Barrick +1.8% but sector remains 30-40% below 2026 peaks
snippet: Senior gold producers clawed back some losses on November 12 as spot gold recovered toward $4,050 after falling as low as $4,013 on inflation-driven selling, with Newmont gaining approximately 1.6% and Barrick advancing 1.8% from their session lows. The partial recovery highlights the ongoing structural discount: even with gold well above $4,000, GDX and GDXJ remain 30-40% below their 2026 peaks — a gap analysts attribute to cost inflation running ahead of revenue, tight junior financing markets, and institutional rotation out of mining equities.

headline: AUSTRALIAN GOLD AND COPPER DRILLS 16M AT 2.3 G/T Au AT EVERGREEN — polymetallic hit adds gold-silver-copper-lead-zinc in NSW
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) reported on November 12 that hole EGRC018 at its Evergreen project near Hillston in New South Wales intersected 16 metres averaging 2.3 g/t gold from 112 metres depth, with associated silver, copper, lead and zinc mineralization that confirms the system's polymetallic character. The company holds $5.9 million in cash, carries no debt, and has three additional holes awaiting assay results — a capital-light position that gives AGC runway to fully define the target without dilution.

headline: SUPER COPPER MAIDEN DRILL: 4/4 HOLES HIT COPPER AT CORDILLERA COBRE CHILE — Atacama porphyry model confirmed, capital needs ahead
snippet: Vancouver-based Super Copper confirmed copper mineralization in all four assayed holes from its maiden drill program at the El Alto target within the Cordillera Cobre Project in Chile's Atacama Region, validating the structural model for a potential porphyry copper system. The analysis notes the binary reality facing all early-stage copper juniors: a fully confirmed geological hit in a Tier-1 copper jurisdiction is a strong foundation, but progressing toward a resource estimate will require substantial additional capital at a time when junior financing is tighter than at any point since 2016.

headline: NORTHERN MINER GOLD DRILL ROUNDUP: DPM LEADS WITH BREVENE BULGARIA — European gold jurisdictions draw attention as Canadian permitting lags
snippet: The Northern Miner's weekly Gold Drill Down roundup for November 12 highlights DPM's Brevene project in Bulgaria as the standout drill result of the week, in a column that tracks the most significant junior gold exploration intercepts across TSX-V and ASX. The selection of a European project as the top result reflects growing investor interest in EU-jurisdiction exploration targets, where established mining codes, favourable geology, and faster permitting timelines are drawing junior capital away from increasingly backlogged Canadian and Australian review processes.
